events.system:
P = 2,2-dimethylpropane
P --[Br₂, hν]--> Q
Q --[CH₃ONa]--> R
R --[HI (1 equiv)]--> S
Q --[Mg, dry ether]--> T
T --[(i) CO₂ (dry ice); (ii) H₃O⁺]--> U
U --[CH₃OH, conc. H₂SO₄ (cat.), heat]--> V
V --[(i) DIBAL-H, 195 K; (ii) H₂O]--> W
events.hidden_link: The student must correctly deduce the structure of neopentyl bromide (Q), realize that ether cleavage of R with HI occurs via SN2 at the less hindered methyl group yielding S as methyl iodide, and track the carbon count when Grignard T reacts with CO2 to form a 6-carbon acid (U).
events.route: 1. Bromination of P yields neopentyl bromide (Q). 2. Williamson ether synthesis gives methyl neopentyl ether (R). 3. Cleavage of R with 1 equiv HI yields methyl iodide (S) because SN2 is favored at the less hindered methyl carbon. 4. Grignard formation (T) and carboxylation adds a carbon, giving 3,3-dimethylbutanoic acid (U). 5. Fischer esterification gives methyl 3,3-dimethylbutanoate (V). 6. DIBAL-H reduction of V yields 3,3-dimethylbutanal (W).
events.student_must_notice: The regioselectivity of the ether cleavage (R to S) where I- attacks the less sterically hindered methyl group, and the carbon chain elongation during the Grignard carboxylation (T to U).
events.trap: Assuming S is neopentyl iodide, or that U is 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid (pivalic acid) by forgetting the CH2 group between the tert-butyl and the newly added carboxyl group.
events.given: The reaction scheme with P named as 2,2-dimethylpropane.
events.asked: Identify the correct statements regarding the intermediate and final compounds.
events.why_hard: It tests both the strict SN2 regioselectivity of ether cleavage on a heavily hindered system and accurate carbon counting during Grignard carboxylation.
events.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the reaction scheme?

options.A: Reaction of R with 1 equivalent of HI yields S as methyl iodide.
options.B: Compound W gives positive Tollens' and Fehling's tests.
options.C: Compound U produces effervescence with aqueous NaHCO₃ and has a degree of unsaturation of 1.

events.stem:
An alkane P is subjected to a sequence of functional group transformations to yield various organic intermediates and products as outlined below.
P = 2,2-dimethylpropane
P --[Br₂, hν]--> Q
Q --[CH₃ONa]--> R
R --[HI (1 equiv)]--> S
Q --[Mg, dry ether]--> T
T --[(i) CO₂ (dry ice); (ii) H₃O⁺]--> U
U --[CH₃OH, conc. H₂SO₄ (cat.), heat]--> V
V --[(i) DIBAL-H, 195 K; (ii) H₂O]--> W
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
(A) The alkyl halide obtained as compound S has the molecular formula CH₃I.
(B) Compound U gives effervescence with aqueous NaHCO₃ solution.
(C) Compound W gives a positive Tollens' test.
(D) The total number of sp³-hybridized carbon atoms in one molecule of compound U is 4.
Choose all the correct options.

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working: P = 2,2-dimethylpropane (neopentane) C(CH3)4. Br2 hv leads to radical bromination giving 1-bromo-2,2-dimethylpropane (primary bromide). Q = primary bromide. CH3ONa (methoxide) induces elimination to give alkene R (most substituted alkene). HI (1 equiv) protonates and then SN2 substitution on primary bromide giving primary iodide CH3I as S. Q also undergoes Grignard formation with Mg in dry ether giving T = organomagnesium bromide of primary bromide (R-Mg-Br). CO2 quench gives carboxylate U = 1-carboxy-2,2-dimethylpropanoate (i.e., 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid after protonation). U with aqueous acid gives carboxylic acid V = 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid. Methanol conc H2SO4 heat gives ester V' (methyl ester) maybe? Actually acid + MeOH/H2SO4 gives ester V = methyl 2,2-dimethylpropanoate. DIBAL-H reduces ester to primary alcohol W = methyl 2,2-dimethylpropanol (i.e., 1-hydroxy-2,2-dimethylpropane). Tollens test requires aldehyde; W is alcohol, negative. U is carboxylic acid, gives effervescence with NaHCO3 (CO2 evolution). Count sp3 carbons in U: U is 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid (CH3)2C(CO2H)CH3? Actually structure: CH3-C(CO2H)(CH3)2? Wait 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid = pentanoic acid with two methyls on C2? That gives 5 carbons all sp3 (including carbonyl carbon is sp2). So sp3 carbons = 4 (excluding carbonyl). Thus D true? Let's check: acid carbonyl carbon is sp2, other four carbons sp3, so total sp3 =4. So D true. However need verify U after CO2 quench and protonation yields acid with carbonyl sp2, yes. So D true. Thus correct statements: A (CH3I), B (effervescence), D (sp3 count 4). C false. So answer AD.

members.name: glm-5.3-flash
members.working: P = neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane). All H equivalent, so Br2/hν gives neopentyl bromide Q = (CH3)3CCH2Br. Q + CH3ONa (SN2) gives neopentyl methyl ether R = (CH3)3CCH2OCH3. HI (1 equiv) cleaves the ether at the methyl side (SN2 on less hindered carbon), giving S = CH3I plus neopentyl alcohol — so (A) is correct. Q + Mg gives neopentyl Grignard T; with CO2 then H3O+ gives U = 3,3-dimethylbutanoic acid, (CH3)3CCH2COOH. Carboxylic acids effervesce with NaHCO3, so (B) is correct. U + CH3OH/H2SO4 gives methyl ester V = (CH3)3CCH2COOCH3. DIBAL-H at 195 K reduces ester to aldehyde W = (CH3)3CCH2CHO (3,3-dimethylbutanal), which gives positive Tollens' test — (C) is correct. In U, sp3 carbons: three CH3 + one quaternary C + one CH2 = 5 sp3 carbons (only COOH carbon is sp2), so (D) is wrong.
